First project-code read that materializes the attacker-controlled fixed local ZIP header body after the start-of-file scan finds the first PK\x03\x04 signature and openArchive skips the 2-byte 'version needed to extract' field. These 24 bytes contain the namelen and extralen fields that drive the short extra-field read.

openArchive passes the requested extra-field length handledextralen instead of the actual byte count returned by dev->read. When the extra-field read is short, parseExtraField is told that unread bytes in buffer are valid input, so it walks past the initialized prefix into uninitialized stack memory. The patch fixes this exact obligation by passing n.

After the start-of-file scan finds the first local ZIP header signature at witness offset 97, openArchive skips the 2-byte version-needed-to-extract field and reads the 24-byte fixed local-header body from offsets 103..126 into buffer. These attacker-controlled bytes carry the namelen and extralen fields used below.
Materializes the filename length from the local-header bytes. In the staged PoC, buffer[20..21] are 0xff 0xff, so namelen becomes 65535.
Materializes the extra-field length from the same header bytes. In the staged PoC, buffer[22..23] are also 0xff 0xff, so extralen becomes 65535.

Consumes namelen bytes as the filename. With namelen=65535, fileName consumes witness offsets 127..65661 inclusive and leaves the device positioned at 65662 in the 65686-byte witness file, so the read succeeds and only 24 bytes remain before EOF for the extra field.
Caps the requested extra-field read to the destination buffer size. With extralen=65535 and sizeof buffer=47, handledextralen becomes 47.

Attempts to read 47 extra-field bytes into buffer, but only witness offsets 65662..65685 remain after the oversized filename. The staged PoC supplies 24 zero bytes here, so n=24, buffer[0..23] become initialized zeros, and buffer[24..46] remain uninitialized stack memory.

Root cause. openArchive ignores the actual byte count n=24 and passes handledextralen=47 to parseExtraField. There is no short-read guard and no reduction of the claimed initialized extent of buffer before parsing begins.

anchors.code: int magic = (uchar)buffer[0] | (uchar)buffer[1] << 8; buffer += 2; int fieldsize = (uchar)buffer[0] | (uchar)buffer[1] << 8; buffer += 2; size -= 4;
anchors.note: parseExtraField starts with size=47. Because the 24 initialized extra-field bytes are all 0x00, the loop interprets them as six zero-length subheaders, advancing buffer by 24 bytes while size falls only to 23. The next iteration therefore decodes the seventh subheader header from buffer[24..27], which were never initialized by dev->read.

MSan sink. On the seventh iteration, fieldsize is assembled from uninitialized buffer[26..27] in the tail of char buffer[47]; after size -= 4, line 270 compares that indeterminate fieldsize against size==19. MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value here, with the origin in KZip::openArchive's stack buffer.
